description: Dated external events that change what someone should do. Not a news feed — every row must survive the 'so what' test.

columns.name: date
columns.note: When the event happened, not when you found it

columns.name: so_what
columns.note: Why a seller should care, in one sentence. REQUIRED. A signal without this is news, and news belongs somewhere else.

columns.name: relevance
columns.note: High means it changes what someone does this week. Reserve it.

columns.name: competitor_id
columns.note: COMP- id when the signal is about a tracked competitor. Set this on every competitor signal — it's what makes the news visible from the competitor registry instead of dead-ending in the market log.

columns.name: competitive_impact
columns.note: What this actually changes about how you sell against them. 'No impact' is a valid and common answer.

columns.name: related_id
columns.note: CUST-/OPP-/LEAD- id. A signal tied to a tracked record is worth an order of magnitude more than a general one.

columns.name: content_reviewed
columns.note: Whether this signal has been assessed as a content opportunity. Drives the 'new since last sweep' list in demand gen.

columns.name: content_opp_id
columns.note: CONTENT- id if this signal produced a piece

columns.name: task_id
columns.note: TASK- id if this produced a task

columns.name: source_type
columns.note: Where this came from. Newsletter items are pre-filtered by an editor who knows the space, which is worth knowing when weighing them.

columns.name: newsletter_name
columns.note: Which publication, when source_type is Newsletter or Feed

columns.name: confidence
columns.note: Confirmed = primary source or company statement. Rumour = single unverified report. Say which.
